decisions.reason: We keep A because the renamed 518 FLEX was given dedicated promotion in both years, built on an already accepted BASIC 518 base, and fits our resource-saving screening portfolio, so management is inclined to justify and continue the investment.

We keep B because the AK flail shredder line was publicly updated to EU Stage V, showing continued technical and regulatory investment in a core mobile product family that management is unlikely to reverse.

We keep C because its move from a simple website mention to its own page signals increasing commitment in a central mobile grinding segment, making early uncertainty easier to interpret as a temporary ramp-up issue.
We drop D because it was only briefly mentioned at launch and then disappeared from the website, so visible commitment is limited and management has less pressure to defend further spending on it.

We keep F because the CERON pre-shredders received sustained standalone promotion and strong public claims of leadership, creating high escalation pressure to persist with a strategically important stationary shredding line.
